explain: Strings are immutable: `trim()` and `toUpperCase()` each **return a new string**, and both results are thrown away. `tag` never changes, so it still has its spaces and its original case. To get `[SALE]` you'd write `tag = tag.trim().toUpperCase();`.

A negative index counts from the end, so `slice(-6)` means *the last 6 characters*: `"Script"`. With no `end`, slice runs to the end of the string. `"TypeS"` would be `slice(0, 5)`; `"cript"` is only 5 characters, `slice(-5)`.

q: `word` might be the empty string `""`. Which expressions are safe (they never throw)? Select all that apply.
explain: On `""`, `word[0]` is `undefined`, and calling `.toUpperCase()` on `undefined` throws a TypeError. `charAt(0)` returns `""` instead, and `slice` simply returns `""` when there's nothing to cut, so the other three are all safe.

q: Which signature is the idiomatic way to type a function that takes some text and returns text?
explain: Lowercase `string` is the primitive type for text. Capital `String` is the type of the wrapper *object*, which you almost never want. `"string"` in quotes is a literal type that only allows that exact word. And TypeScript has no `char` type: a character is just a `string` of length 1.
